requirements.requirement: Provision local accounts designer, reviewer, and visitor.
requirements.summary: All three local accounts were created and remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure designer-created subdirectories and documents inherit reviewer read/write access without periodic permission repair.
requirements.summary: Default POSIX ACLs were applied to the project directory. Nested content created by designer under umask 077 inherited reviewer access, and reviewer directly read, appended to, and created content both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep designer as owner of newly created files and directories.
requirements.summary: Direct stat output shows designer:designer ownership for nested directories and documents created before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Prevent visitor from accessing the project area.
requirements.summary: Visitor listing, reading, and writing attempts were denied before and after restart; ACLs also show no permissions for other users.
The pre-existing brief.txt retained its original SHA-256 checksum, size, inode, ownership, and content checksum through configuration and restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 remained unchanged. The solution used already-installed, functioning POSIX ACL utilities without package or kernel changes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Native default ACL inheritance works for nested designer-created content, reviewer can read and write it, visitor is denied, designer ownership is retained, existing data is preserved, and the platform is unchanged. The mandatory node restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, running recovered state, preserved data and ACLs, and successful post-restart behavior are directly shown and corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: No dedicated scheduler inventory was captured; the absence of a periodic repair job is supported by the complete command timeline and the demonstrated native default-ACL implementation rather than a direct cron/timer listing.
The lifecycle collector does not inventory /var/tmp, so retention of the boot-ID marker is inferred from its creation and use without a recorded cleanup command.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The state-changing commands were causally connected to account provisioning, ACL configuration, bounded functional testing, or the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services, new listeners, or package damage appeared afterward. Low-risk evidence scratch files were unnecessarily retained: /tmp/visitor.out and /tmp/visitor.err from cmd-0bd422d61ca940b3, /tmp/visitor-post.out and /tmp/visitor-post.err from cmd-38ac798fb6624b72, and apparently the /var/tmp boot-ID marker created by cmd-91285a84983a424e. These were not shown cleaned; the lifecycle snapshot directly confirms the four /tmp files. The test project hierarchy remained, but it served as bounded final and post-restart evidence rather than an unrelated mutation.
